biography.plain_text: Daniel K. Ludwig was an American shipping magnate who built National Bulk Carriers into a major tanker owner. Starting with a loan backed by his father, he developed charter-based financing and larger ships that generated a vast fortune. His business interests later extended into mining, property, hotels and other industries.

long_biography.plain_text:
Shipping magnate Daniel Ludwig created the Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research in 1971, endowing it with most of his international business holdings. He wanted scientists in different countries to have dependable support for work that might take decades, insulated from changes in public interest and government policy. His will extended that commitment to American research institutions.

Ludwig's shipbuilding methods reflected his early training in marine engineering. After working as a ship supplier, he studied mathematics at night and trained with Fairbanks, Morse, installing engines before establishing his own business. At Japan's Kure shipyard, he used prefabricated sections to streamline construction. Standardised designs made components interchangeable and allowed crews to move between ships with familiar equipment.
long_biography.html:
Shipping magnate Daniel Ludwig created the Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research in 1971, endowing it with most of his international business holdings. He wanted scientists in different countries to have dependable support for work that might take decades, insulated from changes in public interest and government policy. His will extended that commitment to American research institutions.

Ludwig's shipbuilding methods reflected his early training in marine engineering. After working as a ship supplier, he studied mathematics at night and trained with Fairbanks, Morse, installing engines before establishing his own business. At Japan's Kure shipyard, he used prefabricated sections to streamline construction. Standardised designs made components interchangeable and allowed crews to move between ships with familiar equipment.
